title: The Real Cost of Employee Turnover
titleZh: 員工流動率的真實成本
illustrationIdea: An HR manager stands at a whiteboard where one small labelled box marked 'recruiting ads' sits above a much larger iceberg of hidden costs, while warehouse workers move pallets in the background.

paragraphs.en: When Harper Lin took over human resources at Vellmore Logistics, she inherited a problem nobody wanted to name. The warehouse division lost nearly a third of its staff every year, yet the annual [[budget]] recorded that loss as a single modest line: recruitment advertising. Harper suspected the real figure was hiding elsewhere. For three months she traced every [[expense]] that one departure set in motion. The total she carried into the board meeting was nine times what management had assumed.
paragraphs.zh: 當 Harper Lin 接下 Vellmore Logistics 的人資主管一職時，她也接手了一個沒人願意講明的問題。倉儲部門每年流失將近三分之一的員工，但年度預算卻只把這筆損失記成一行不起眼的項目：徵才廣告費。Harper 懷疑真正的數字藏在別的地方。她花了三個月，把一名員工離職所連帶引發的每一筆支出都追查出來。她帶進董事會的總額，是管理層原本估計的九倍。

paragraphs.en: The visible costs came first. Posting a [[vacancy]], screening [[applicants]], and running interviews ate manager hours that nobody ever billed to a department. Agency fees for licensed forklift operators reached twelve percent of a first-year [[salary]]. Then came paperwork, uniforms, and the safety training every newcomer finished before touching a machine. Together these reached about four thousand dollars per [[hire]] — uncomfortable, but not shocking. The second half of the report was the part that silenced the room.
paragraphs.zh: 看得見的成本最先浮現。刊登職缺、篩選應徵者、安排面試，吃掉了主管大量工時，而這些時間從來沒被算進任何部門的帳上。透過仲介找有證照的堆高機操作員，仲介費高達第一年薪水的一成二。接著是文件作業、制服，以及每位新人碰到機器前必須完成的安全訓練。這些加起來，每雇用一人約四千美元——讓人不舒服，但還不到驚人的地步。真正讓會議室安靜下來的，是報告的後半部。

paragraphs.en: While a position sits empty, the work does not pause. The remaining staff absorb the extra [[shifts]], and [[overtime]] pay climbs with them. Harper found that the night crew worked nine additional hours a week during vacancies, all at a premium rate, and [[productivity]] fell anyway. Tired workers packed more orders incorrectly, and every wrong shipment meant freight charges and apologies. One regional [[client]] cancelled a [[contract]] worth six hundred thousand dollars after three late deliveries.
paragraphs.zh: 職缺空著的時候，工作並不會跟著停下。留下來的人得吸收多出來的班次，加班費也跟著往上爬。Harper 發現，缺人期間夜班人員平均每週多做九小時，而且全是加成計費；生產力卻還是下滑。疲勞的員工包錯更多訂單，每一次出貨錯誤都意味著運費支出與道歉。一家區域客戶在三次延遲交貨後，取消了一紙價值六十萬美元的合約。

paragraphs.en: Then there is the slow climb of the [[replacement]]. A new forklift operator needed eleven weeks to match the output of the person who left; a shift [[supervisor]] needed seven months. Throughout that stretch the company pays a full [[wage]] for partial performance, and no accounting column exists for the difference. Harper described it to the board as paying the full price for a truck that could only be driven half loaded.
paragraphs.zh: 接著是接替者緩慢爬升的那段期間。新的堆高機操作員需要十一週才能追上離職者的產出，輪班主管則要七個月。這段期間公司付的是全額工資，換來的卻是部分產能，而會計科目裡根本沒有這一欄。Harper 向董事會形容：這等於用全額價錢買一輛卡車，卻只能載半車貨。

paragraphs.en: The effect on those who stay may be the costliest item of all. [[Morale]] drops as familiar faces disappear, workloads grow, and every [[resignation]] quietly invites [[colleagues]] to weigh their own options. Two supervisors admitted they had started returning recruiters' calls only after watching their best packers leave. Departures, in short, lead to more departures, until a division that once trained newcomers has nobody experienced enough to teach them.
paragraphs.zh: 對留下來的人造成的影響，或許才是最貴的一項。熟面孔一個個消失，士氣下滑、工作量變重，而每一次辭職都在無聲地邀請同事評估自己的去留。兩位主管坦承，是在看著手下最好的包裝員離開之後，他們才開始回獵才顧問的電話。換句話說，離職會製造更多離職，直到一個曾經有能力訓練新人的部門，再也找不到夠資深的人來教。

paragraphs.en: Why do companies tolerate such an expensive habit? Harper's answer was structural. The cost of [[turnover]] is scattered across the organization, and no single manager owns the total. Agency fees sit in human resources, overtime sits in operations, lost accounts sit in sales, and the training burden falls on whoever stands nearest. Turnover therefore looks cheap to everyone and expensive to nobody.
paragraphs.zh: 公司為什麼容忍這種昂貴的習慣？Harper 的答案是結構性的。人員流動的成本被打散在整個組織裡，沒有任何一位主管扛得起這個總數。仲介費掛在人資、加班費掛在營運、丟掉的客戶算在業務、訓練負擔則落在離得最近的人身上。人員流動因此對每個人來說都很便宜，對誰都不算貴。

paragraphs.en: What Harper proposed was nothing dramatic: schedules published three weeks ahead, a modest [[bonus]] at the twelve-month mark, permission for supervisors to approve shift swaps without calling headquarters, and exit interviews run by an outsider. The package cost two hundred thousand dollars a year. Eighteen months later, warehouse departures had fallen from thirty-four percent to nineteen, [[retention]] among second-year staff had nearly doubled, and the division's operating [[margin]] had risen a full point.
paragraphs.zh: Harper 提出的做法一點也不華麗：班表提前三週公布、滿一年發一筆小額獎金、主管可自行核准換班不必請示總部、離職面談由外部人員來做。整包措施一年約花二十萬美元。十八個月後，倉儲部門的離職比例從三成四降到一成九，第二年員工的留任率幾乎翻倍，部門的營業利潤率也上升了一個百分點。

questions.q: What is the main point of the article?
options: Employment agencies charge fees that most companies cannot afford.
Warehouse positions are harder to fill than office positions.
Most of what staff departures cost a company is never recorded as a cost of turnover.
Exit interviews are the only reliable way to measure satisfaction at work.
questions.explanation: 第一段點出帳上只有「徵才廣告費」一行，實際總額卻是九倍；第六段解釋成本被打散到各部門。全文主線就是「真實成本從未以流動成本的名義被記錄」。

questions.q: According to Harper's findings, what happened while positions were left unfilled?
options: The night crew worked about nine extra hours a week at a higher rate.
Managers cut the number of night shifts in order to save money.
The company borrowed workers from another division.
Customers agreed to accept later delivery dates.
questions.explanation: 定位第三段：缺人期間夜班人員每週多做九小時，且全部按加成費率計算。其他選項文中都沒有提到。

questions.q: Harper's comparison to a truck that can only be driven half loaded suggests that
options: the company's vehicles were too old for heavy work.
new workers should be given smaller machines at first.
safety training programs are usually far too short.
full pay is being spent on output that is still incomplete.
questions.explanation: 推論題，定位第四段：公司付全額工資，但新人只交出部分產能，比喻的重點在「付全價、卻只得到一半的效果」。

questions.q: What can be inferred about why managers rarely act on this cost?
options: Company law forbids recording such losses in the accounts.
No department sees the whole figure, so the problem never looks urgent.
Most managers believe workers cannot be persuaded to stay.
Boards refuse to approve any spending on staff benefits.
questions.explanation: 推論題，定位第六段：費用分散在人資、營運、業務與訓練之中，沒有人扛總數，因此「對每個人都很便宜」，自然不會有人動手處理。

questions.q: What does the outcome of Harper's plan suggest?
options: Fairly cheap changes to working conditions can return more than they cost.
Raising wages is the only way to keep warehouse staff.
Companies should change supervisors every eighteen months.
Operating results depend mainly on advertising spending.
questions.explanation: 推論題，定位第七段：一年二十萬美元的樸素措施，換來離職率減半與利潤率上升一個百分點，可推知投入不高的條件改善其實划算。

title: Why Subscription Boxes Keep Failing
titleZh: 訂閱制電商為何總是難以獲利
illustrationIdea: A founder sits on the floor of a half-empty warehouse surrounded by unshipped gift boxes, holding a single bag of coffee beans and looking at a wall chart where the subscriber line drops month by month.

paragraphs.en: In its first spring, Harvest Crate looked unstoppable. Nadia Reyes had left a marketing job to mail monthly boxes of unusual food — chili honey, seaweed crackers, single-origin chocolate — to anyone curious enough to sign up. Within eight months she had eleven thousand [[subscribers]] and two [[investors]] willing to pay for a larger [[warehouse]]. Within three years the company was closed. The explanation had been sitting in the numbers since the very first month.
paragraphs.zh: 在創業的第一個春天，Harvest Crate 看起來勢不可擋。Nadia Reyes 辭掉行銷工作，每月寄出裝滿新奇食品的箱子——辣味蜂蜜、海苔脆餅、單一產區巧克力——寄給任何一個好奇到願意訂閱的人。八個月內，她累積了一萬一千名訂閱者，還有兩位投資人願意出錢換更大的倉庫。三年之內，公司卻收了。答案其實從第一個月起就躺在數字裡。

paragraphs.en: Every subscription business starts with the same arithmetic. Harvest Crate gave fifty percent off the opening box, and each new member cost about thirty-eight dollars in [[advertising]] to attract. Add that [[discount]], the goods inside, and the [[shipping]], and the first box lost roughly twenty dollars. Nothing was wrong with that by itself. The company simply had to hold on to the customer for five months before it saw any [[profit]].
paragraphs.zh: 每一門訂閱生意都從同一道算術開始。Harvest Crate 首箱打五折，而每吸引一名新會員，廣告成本約三十八美元。再加上折扣、箱內商品與運費，第一箱大約虧二十美元。這件事本身沒有問題，只是公司必須把這位客戶留住五個月，才開始看得到任何利潤。

paragraphs.en: Most customers did not stay that long. Half had [[cancelled]] by the fourth month. Nadia had built a discovery box, and discovery has a short life: the first jar of unfamiliar jam is a delight, the fifth is a problem on the shelf. The subscriptions that survive tend to sell what people were going to buy anyway — coffee, razor blades, pet food, contact lenses — because a [[loyal]] customer stops paying only when the need itself stops.
paragraphs.zh: 多數客戶沒撐那麼久。到第四個月，已有一半的人取消。Nadia 做的是「探索型」箱子，而新鮮感的壽命很短：第一罐沒吃過的果醬是驚喜，第五罐就成了櫃子上的難題。活得下來的訂閱制，通常賣的是人們本來就會買的東西——咖啡、刮鬍刀片、寵物食品、隱形眼鏡——因為忠實客戶只有在需求本身消失時才會停止付錢。

paragraphs.en: The second trap was the calendar. Boxes are planned six to ten weeks ahead, so [[inventory]] must be bought before anyone knows how many members will remain, and [[demand]] can be estimated but never known. Nadia's [[forecast]] for one December assumed fourteen thousand boxes; she sent nine thousand. The surplus sat in storage until the dates on the jars ran out. Order too little instead, and substitutions begin — and substitutions produce complaints.
paragraphs.zh: 第二個陷阱是時間表。箱子必須提前六到十週規劃，因此庫存得在沒人知道會剩下多少會員之前就先買進，而需求只能估計、無法確知。Nadia 某年十二月的預測是一萬四千箱，實際只寄出九千箱，多出來的貨躺在倉儲裡，直到罐子上的有效期限過去。反過來訂太少，就得改用替代品；而替代品換來的是客訴。

paragraphs.en: Then there is weight. Eight jars and tins travel heavily, and postage plus [[packaging]] consumed twenty-two percent of Harvest Crate's [[revenue]]. Nadia tried to [[negotiate]] better rates with carriers, though the volume needed for a real reduction was still far away. Worse, her [[suppliers]] had given samples away gladly while the box worked as free promotion; once she wanted steady quantities, they quoted ordinary [[wholesale]] prices.
paragraphs.zh: 再來是重量。八個玻璃罐和鐵罐運起來很沉，郵資加上包裝材料吃掉了 Harvest Crate 兩成二的營收。Nadia 試著和物流業者協商更好的費率，但要換到真正的折讓，需要的出貨量還遠遠不夠。更糟的是，當這個箱子還算免費宣傳時，供應商都樂意免費提供樣品；一旦她要穩定的數量，對方報的就是一般批發價。

paragraphs.en: The models that last look duller. They carry one line of goods rather than a surprise, they set a [[retail]] price high enough to absorb [[delivery]], and they often own what they sell instead of passing along someone else's brand. A coffee company that roasts its own beans keeps the maker's share as well as the seller's; [[competitors]] who merely assemble other people's products are left with whatever is still on the table after everyone has been paid.
paragraphs.zh: 撐得久的模式看起來反而無趣得多。它們只做一條產品線而不是驚喜包，訂的零售價高到足以吸收配送成本，而且賣的往往是自家的東西，而不是轉手別人的品牌。自己烘豆的咖啡商，同時賺到製造端與銷售端的那一份；而只是把別人的商品組裝成箱的競爭對手，只能拿到所有人分完之後桌上剩下的部分。

paragraphs.en: Nadia's second company sells one thing — her own roasted coffee, sent every three weeks, cancel whenever you like. No theme, no mystery, no surprise. The [[launch]] cost a few thousand dollars, and the business turned profitable in fourteen months with a fifth of the customers she once had. The box, she says now, was never the product. The habit was, and habits are built on what people already want, arriving before they run out.
paragraphs.zh: Nadia 的第二家公司只賣一樣東西——她自己烘的咖啡，每三週寄一次，隨時可以取消。沒有主題、沒有懸念、沒有驚喜。這次上市只花了幾千美元，卻在十四個月內轉為獲利，客戶數只有當年的五分之一。她現在說，箱子從來就不是產品，習慣才是；而習慣建立在人們本來就想要、而且會在用完之前準時送到的東西上。

questions.q: What does the article identify as the central problem with boxes like Harvest Crate?
options: Customers dislike receiving food through the post.
The cost of winning a member is repaid only after several months, and most members leave first.
Investors refuse to put money into this kind of company.
Food products are too heavy to be sold online at all.
questions.explanation: 定位第二、三段：首箱虧約二十美元，要留住客戶五個月才開始獲利，但到第四個月已有一半取消。主旨即在這個時間差。

questions.q: How much of Harvest Crate's revenue went to postage and packaging?
options: Twelve percent
Fifty percent
Thirty-eight percent
Twenty-two percent
questions.explanation: 細節題，定位第五段明寫二成二。五十％是首箱折扣、三十八美元是廣告獲客成本，屬於干擾選項。

questions.q: What changed in Harvest Crate's relationship with its suppliers as the company grew?
options: They stopped treating the box as free promotion and began charging normal prices.
They asked for a share of the monthly membership fees.
They refused to work with food companies of any kind.
They moved their goods to a competing box instead.
questions.explanation: 定位第五段：箱子還算免費宣傳時供應商樂意送樣品，等到她需要穩定數量，對方就報一般批發價。

questions.q: Why does the writer mention coffee, razor blades and pet food?
options: They are cheaper to send than jars of jam.
They were the products Harvest Crate refused to carry.
They are bought again and again out of need, so members have little reason to stop.
They can be produced without any suppliers.
questions.explanation: 推論題，定位第三段：這些例子是用來對比「探索型」箱子，說明補貨型商品的需求持續，客戶不會因為新鮮感消失而取消。

questions.q: What does the closing idea — that the box was never the product — suggest?
options: Buyers care more about package design than about the goods inside.
A successful service depends on careful selection and surprise.
A company should offer as many product lines as it can manage.
A subscription works when it supplies something the buyer would keep purchasing anyway.
questions.explanation: 推論題，定位第七段並呼應第三段：第二家公司只賣自家咖啡、定期補貨，說明真正撐住訂閱的是既有需求所形成的習慣，而非開箱的驚喜。
